title: Timestamp option for habit completions
body:

One feature we’d really love to see is the ability to add or edit a timestamp for each habit completion. This would make the history much more accurate, especially when we forget to mark a habit right away.

For example, if I go to the gym at 6 PM but only check it off at 9 PM, I’d like to set the completion time to 6 PM so the habit history reflects when it actually happened.

This would be a very useful feature and would make the app even more valuable for us. Thanks again!

One thing I noticed that others implement that I can’t figure out how to do here is if I miss something that I’m supposed to do every X days (for instance), I don’t get an indication that I missed the habit beyond looking at the previous day’s ring.

author: Mme Azizam

title: Awesome Habits. Awesome App.
body:
Every time I start with a new productivity system I over complicate it. Not with this. Empty rings bad. Filled rings good. Habits are incredibly simple to set up and customize. Back filling is easy and day/week/month views are great. The widgets put habits front and center and performing a habit has become a welcome alternative to getting swept up in social media. 

With my setup, a “meh” day means about 70%— C work, but a better baseline (and better streaks!) than I’ve had in the past. 100% days really count and include a mix of baseline habits, tracked dietary needs, and other positive activities. 

I only have two (minor) complaints:
- You can seemingly only change the primary ring color by changing the app to mono. Can we please set the primary ring color separately?
- Similarly, you can’t set colors on lists, so you have to manage lists and colors separately. List colors, still separate from individual habit colors but with the option to apply to all habits, would be hugely appreciated. 

Wishlist:
- Expanding on the above, a view with a circle for each list’s progress with respective colors + an icon for each
- Mark a habit as “Bonus” so it contributes to the total percentage in a way that can exceed 100%

My recommendation— Get it. There are similar apps out there, but none that balance simplicity and functionality in such a satisfyingly iOS-like way.

title: Intuitive, and powerful
body:
When I first loaded this app, it was almost easy to mistake it for any other habit tracker because of it doesn’t try to overcomplicate the user with too many features. But if you dig deeper, the amount of customization and power sets this app apart from the others. 

Pros: 
 - Clean simple design. 
- Lots of customization of your habit list. 
- Fast cross device syncing. 
- Widgets have lots of options and sizes. 
- Can show the live habit timer inside a widget. 
- Live activities for habit timers. 
- Apps for every Apple device including MacOS. 
- Add urls or Apple Shortcuts to habits to quick launch whatever you want. 
- Apple Shortcut actions with almost full control over everything in the app. 

As an example power feature, you can use quick launch on a habit to launch an Apple Shortcut which marks the habit as complete, and then launches whatever else you want, creating a perfect automation companion for your habits. 

Cons: 
- The app needs to open for every Apple Shortcut action you launch. I really hope the developer can make this work in the background so Apple Shortcut Personal Automations will work with my phone locked. 
- More widget options couldn’t hurt, like having one for a “up next” habit which shows the next goal in your habit list for the day. 

As you can see, the cons are extremely minor, this app deserves five stars even despite those. Highly recommend this app if you are looking for a simple yet powerful habit app.

title: Great UI and UX!
body:
A lot of thought went into this app and it shows. So easy to use and a pleasant experience to mark goals complete. Tap the widget, tap the goal, and done. Or use Siri Shortcuts. This is perfect.

I was wondering if you have a roadmap anywhere on what improvements might be coming down the pipe. Some apps have an entire week view with little colored or uncolered squares showing if a goal was completed. It’s a cool way to pack a lot of data, like 10 goals over a week, and view it all at once.

Another cool feature would be multi level goals to track workouts, like the habit could be bench press, the # of reps would another dimension, and the weight would be the 3rd level dimension. Getting data in for weight and reps would mean you completed the goal of bench press, but would be cool to track weight and reps in a way that could be displayed on graphs. So not just using the notes feature for this.

Lastly, for the hardcore nerds among us, csv export of all the data in case we want to juxtapose our goals alongside data from other apps that we are tracking. Like overlaying our goals data on a graph from our smart scale app that shows our weight/ muscle mass/etc. exporting the data makes this possible and allows for the potential to make some amazing insights on how our habits can correlate to other things that we are tracking.

This app should become the solution to track everything else. We have Apple Watch and smart scales to track so many things, overlaying that data on top of anything else we want to track should make this a must have app.

author: chels0876497

title: A fairly viable Streaks alternative
body:
Some things it shares with Streaks:

- Just recently, it added the ability to attach a URL to a habit.

Here’s what it has over Streaks right now:

- Unlimited habits. You aren’t limited to 24.

- Habit categorization: via lists, which operate like tags, meaning you can add multiple lists to one habit

- The ability to add units past a goal

  - With Streaks, once you get the habit done, that’s it. You can’t, say, add one more hour to a Play Piano habit because you already hit your goal.

  - Awesome let’s you add more hours even when you hit your goal, making it more close to Strides in tracking.

- Just recently, it added the ability to attach a description to a habit.

Here’s where it lacks:

- It’s library of Apple Health synced habits is still limited when compared to Streaks. I don’t believe I can sync things like tooth brushing.

- You can only run one timer at once and it must be done while the app is still open. If you exit the screen, the timer will stop.

- Lack of badges. You’ll have to enter the app each time to know how many habits you have yet to complete.

- The only way to filter habits is via lists. You can’t text search them or filter them by status yet.

title: Very nice so far, with a couple suggestions
body:
I haven't been using the app for very long yet, but after trying a number of habit tracking apps trying to find one that works for me I am enjoying this one. Pleasing interface, simple yet varied habit type setup, easy to use and nice apple watch app and widgets. There are a couple of things I'm missing that other apps had though:
1. The ability to set a habit for "every x days," such as for something I want to do every 3 days as opposed to on specific days of the week. I unexpectedly found this very helpful on other apps so I'm missing it now.
2. Snoozing habits. There's a skip button but if you're traveling it could be a pain to have to skip habits every day that you can't do while away from home. Maybe archiving & then un-archiving could do this? I haven't had a need to try it yet.
3. This one isn't something I expect to change, but I do wish more habit apps had a visual monthly overview of what days you completed what habits. I'm a visual person when it comes to tracking time and also have a hard time remembering when I did or didn't do things. I'd find some kind of overall calendar view much more useful than a line graph, but I know not everyone is the same. There is a streaks chart of sorts for this using lines for individual habits so that's better than nothing.
4. I meant to stop at 3 but I just remembered: can there be a way to not include habit breaking apps in the daily status ring? I have a simple 'eat fewer sweets' habit set to 3 sweets max but it means i always start my day with the ring partially completed, which feels counterintuitive. I'd rather just not include habit breaking habits in the status ring at all, or have them hurt it somehow if you go over instead of making it look like you already did something at the start of the day.

That said, here are some things that I think would make the app better, from most to least important:
1. Enable a badge counter for number of goals remaining in a day. Making that red number badge go down is very motivating. (Habit has this)

The layout is visually-appealing, and since I’ve always got my phone on me, it’s much more convenient (and fun!) to log data than on paper.

I do have a suggestion for a future update of the app:
Each habit shows a streak of how many days you have kept up with the habit. I think it would be nice to add in a feature that gives a special message whenever you hit certain milestones, especially for daily goals.
We usually get excited about goals when we first set them, and then after a few weeks the excitement wears off. But I think if every now and then if the app gave me a thumbs up for sticking with a goal for 30 days, 3 months, 6 months etc., that would be even better.

I could also just do it myself on a calendar, but I just thought I’d put the suggestion out there. Great app!

body: This app has a lot of great features and meshes well with how I want to think about building and breaking habits. I love the Apple Watch integration and that they don’t go too overboard with analytics, letting you easily see progress without over thinking things. My one request would be to allow users to import more data from health to track things like macronutrients or sleep, but I’m overall satisfied with the app as it is now.

author: Livre-lover

title: Perfect in every way
body: I’ve never reviewed an app before, but I had to come here to gush about how amazing this app is. I’ve tried so, so many habit trackers... some paid, some free, some that took me hours to set up. I’ve been using apps for habit tracking for about 3 years, and probably tried at least 20 apps, and there’s always something not quite right. So this morning I downloaded this app and THIS IS IT. There is just so much to like, but I will try to summarize: the option to have completed tasks move automatically to the bottom of the list, so you can glance at the top to see what to do next (why is this not always a thing?!) ...how it groups tasks by frequency (daily, weekly, monthly) so you can see clearly what you have to do today, but *still see your other tasks too* (this alone makes Awesome Habits better than all the competition, because you don’t have to assign a specific day of the week to see your weekly/monthly tasks in the standard view). The actually functional status ring that lets me choose whether I want to track only today’s tasks or all of them — so having weekly tasks doesn’t have to mean you’re never “done” with everything.  AND, if that wasn’t enough, it is not only iPhone, iPad, Watch (and Mac!) compatible, but the different apps are all thoughtfully done and the syncing is GREAT. It has Watch complications that show the status ring  % complete for the day, and it actually syncs, and fast, between your devices. The iPhone app even has widgets that I actually want to use! It’s beautiful to look at, customizable but still simple, does everything I want and things I didn’t even know I wanted, but has no extra bulk or fluff. And finally — you choose to pay a reasonable one-time fee instead of a subscription. This app is good enough that I would maybe even consider a subscription, but the option to pay once makes this a no-brainer to me. If I could give more stars I would. Totally life changing. Thank you so much for creating this.

author: mbcv38

title: love habits!
body: this is a really clean, well-designed app! i looked at a bunch of apps in this category, but i was sold on this one by both its design and simple pricing model. there's an iOS and Mac version, and both have widgets too, which makes it easy to notice your target goals and log them when completed, all of which syncs across devices without having to create or log in to a separate account. i downloaded this at the start of the new year and it's amazing how many rings i've been able to close every day! a great support for desired behavior changes. i highly recommend it!
author: beizho

title: Great app, two missing features
body:
I love this app. It’s the prettiest of all habit trackers I’ve tried, and I like how habits are arranged in daily and weekly goals (instead of calendar days, as in other apps, which is annoying). I love that it has a Mac app which also works great. I cannot give full points for these two reasons:

- checking off a task involves two clicks: one of the task and another one within the task options. Swipe actions (or one click actions) would be appreciated.

- No watch app!! This is major. I love tracking everything on my watch.

I am still using the app because it works well and it is visually appealing, but I am on the market for another. However, if my two points above were fixed I would stop looking for alternatives.

title: Good way to build/break habits
body: Like most humans, I start things and sometime i finish them. I needed something to keep me on track and motivated, as well as to show progress, no matter how small. Reminders in a busy day is a great tool to stay on track. Seeing the progress on goals/habits is a big motivator. Easy to setup, and follow along. App crashed a few times during deleting some notifications, but I'm assuming as this app gets more users, and updates, the bugs will be quashed. I recommend this app to anyone who wants some support in achieving their goals.
